why: An expression of a class keeps it (MATLAB doc 'Object Arrays', 'Concatenating Objects'): `k = [k, ...` / `Gizmo()]` over a continuation line (a continuation or a comment in the brackets is no element), `k = k(end:-1:1)'` and `k = k.'` (a transpose of an index), `k = [k, w]` with `w` another `Gizmo`, `k = [k(1), k(2)]`: each `tidy(k)` is the class's method (doc 'Function Precedence Order'). A concatenation with `k` itself among its elements keeps the class (project rule, step 15 round 7): MATLAB gives the class, or the class's own concatenation runs, or it errors (MATLAB R2026a: `[k, 1]` and objects of two classes error), so after `k = [k, 1]` or `k = [k, w]` with `w` a `Widget` the call is reached with the object or not at all, and `tidy(k)` is the class's method.
